welcome: What’s your plan in this position? Choose a candidate move and consider Black’s reply.
default: Name a candidate move and your expected reply. You can check the move on a separate board.
hint: Look at your undeveloped pieces and your king. Which move would help one of them? Try forming a plan before calculating a long line.
quiet: I’ll hold notes until you ask for help.
example: This example covers development and castling. Your game is unchanged.
newGame: I’ll observe until you ask for help.
position: White to move. How would you use your king in this endgame?
afterMove: After {reply}, which of your pieces needs attention? Name a candidate move before calculating.
What did {reply} change? Check threats, open lines, and undefended pieces.
Consider your reply to {reply}. What is your opponent’s strongest response to your candidate?
reflection: What were you trying to achieve with that move? A short explanation helps me distinguish your plan from the result.
feedback: Feedback noted in this conversation. Prompt editing is not connected in this prototype.

demonstration.title: Bring your pieces into the game

steps.title: Start with the centre
steps.note: Before moving, find your king and your undeveloped pieces. A useful opening plan usually helps both.

steps.title: Make room
steps.note: 1. e4 e5 opens lines for the bishops and queen. The pawn moves also contest central squares.

steps.title: Develop with a purpose
steps.note: 2. Nf3 attacks the e5 pawn. Black develops a knight to defend it. Each move has a concrete job.

steps.title: Get the king safe
steps.note: 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. O-O. Castling moves the king away from the centre and brings the rook closer to the game. O-O is kingside castling.
